lines.en: It takes a lot to humble a person. Sometimes, even a death.
Which isn’t to say Yumi’s mother had already died. There’s no need to fret about that just yet.
But it was this brush with death and the first taste of its breath as it leans in for a kiss that had started to change her in a way.
It wasn’t a big way. She still thought she was better than everyone. She still wanted to be left alone.
But every once in a while, there would be a less self-destructive thought. Normally about a thing she hopes to do or see or just experience before her time here comes to an end.
This complicated things though, because she didn’t know if her life could come to an end anymore.
So sometimes, after the last bell rang, she’d wander the halls of the school in circles, trying to circumnavigate her head in addition to the third floor.
Sometimes, it’d led her right back home. Sometimes, to work.
But on this particular day, it led her somewhere else.
: Oh, Yumi. There you are.
Today, she’d be led to another princess — one far closer to the title than Yumi ever felt because she’d seen several men have their fingers lopped off by now. And Touka probably hadn’t.
: You left last period before I had a chance to get your attention. What are your plans now that school has ended?
: Yumi?
: Why are you talkin’ to me? We don’t talk. This is weird.
: I apologize if my presence is somewhat of an annoyance to you. I was just operating under the assumption that you’d want money as being poor seems to be quite detrimental to your attitude.
: Ya know, I’ve shaken down my fair share of girls for lunch money before, but this has gotta be the first time one has just come over without me even lifting a finger.
: Please don’t hit me. I am merely a messenger today.
: And now shit’s somehow even weirder. Listen, I know I’m technically Yakuza and shit, but I don’t go around doing collections. So if you’re trying to pass over somebody’s protection money-
: I assure you this has nothing to do with protection money. Unless Tsukasa has decided to take your business idea in a new and rather odd direction.
: Tsukasa? Business? You mean-
: You’re still owed $10,000, are you not? I’ve been asked to finalize the transaction today. Which would require you to accompany me to the manor for a brief-
: Yeah, whatever the fuck you want, I’ll do it. Throw me in a god damn dumpster for all I care. $10k is $10k. I ain’t gonna argue.
: Is $10,000 really such an extravagant amount to you that you’d throw yourself in the trash for it?
: Yes.
: Oh. Is your family just...not very good at being Yakuza then? Because that really does not seem like much to me.
: I don’t fuckin’ take my dad’s filthy money. Most of the time at least. So just point me in the direction of your god damn manor, cause I figured I was just never gettin’ this payout at all.
: There’s a limo waiting outside that’ll take us there together. But if that makes you uncomfortable-
: Nope. Where the fuck’s this limo? Courtyard? On my way.
: Wow...all this obedience for pocket change?
: I wonder if this is how kidnapping works?
: Do you really come to school in this fuckin’ thing every day? Why don’t you just walk? Too good for that or something?
: My mother doesn’t want me walking to school. She says I’d attract too large of a ransom if someone were to swipe me off the sidewalk.
: Weird. Figured there wasn’t any number “too large” for your family.
: There isn’t, which is how I know she’s lying for the sake of my safety.
: I do still walk to school sometimes, though. And I haven’t been stolen yet. So I must be doing something right.
: Pfft. Probably because we ain’t got a rapist as a teacher anymore. Guarantee you you’d be singin’ a different tune if Sensei was still around.
: You say that as if he doesn’t know where I live.
: Probably just forgot. You know how that guy is.
: If it ain’t him, it’d be somebody else though. Your mom’s probably right to keep you away from doin’ shit that could put you in danger. Mine would throw me to the god damn wolves for a six-pack.
: Something tells me you’d have no trouble defending yourself from a few wolves if it really came down to that, Yumi.
: Yeah, and something tells me you’ve got snipers on every building in Kumon-mi ready to blast out the brains of any dude who so much as talks to you.
: Oh, heavens no.
: There are several blind spots the snipers can’t reach. I just need to make sure I avoid them.
: Nice. Real comforting knowing I’m one sneeze away from getting shot.
: Just don’t sneeze and everything will be fine then.
: Besides, I’m in just as much danger as you are right now. Mother makes it sound as if your family is a much bigger deal than you make them out to be.
: They probably are. Means nothing to me, though. I don’t want to get wrapped up in any of that bullshit.
: Understandable. But it doesn’t change the fact that anyone who’d harm even a single hair on your head would wind up with a target on their back.
: Not anyone. Just the ones who haven’t fucked my dad.
: Well, unless your father has secretly been Sensei this whole time, I can’t imagine that cancels out that many people.
: Ew. Don’t even joke about that. You’ve seen his fuckin’ niece-daughter thing. I wouldn’t wish that dude’s fatherhood on anybody.
: Hmm...
: Perhaps he just needs a mother’s help then?
: What he needs is a fuckin’ vasectomy. Maybe a lobotomy too. Think there’s some kinda procedure where you can knock out both of those things at once?
: Heh...I’m not sure. But I’ll keep an eye out...
: God damn....has your place always been this big?
: You’ve been here before, haven’t you? Dorm Wars. Christmas.
: Never through the main entrance. And I definitely ain’t ever seen whatever that fuckin’ part of the house is.
: Ahh, yes. You must be looking at the pleasure wing.
: The what now?
: This manor’s been around for quite a while, Yumi. And it wasn’t uncommon centuries ago for courtesans to be housed within the grounds for...easier access.
: What you’re looking at is the remnants of that. And exactly where we’re going today.
: On second thought, I would like to leave.
: Hahah! Oh, don’t worry. It’s mostly just miscellaneous rooms in there now. We don’t have courtesans anymore.
: There is a private massage room, though. But I wouldn’t recommend going there unless you want to come out with a little less dignity than you had going in.
: Uhh...yeah. I’m good. Thanks. Wh...Why are we going there, though? Ain’t you just gonna give me my money and tell me to fuck off or something?
: After a brief meeting, I presume. I told you — I’m merely a messenger today. It’s my mother who summoned you here. She’s the one you’ll want to direct your questions to.
: Your mom? You mean that rich lady from the Shark Tank thing? I’ve got to talk to her? Why do we need to get adults involved at all? Just give me the cash and tell me to beat it.
: I apologize, Yumi. But I’m afraid I can’t do that.
: Now, follow me. I’ll guide you to the secondary meeting room.
: But once we arrive, you’re on your own...
It takes a lot to humble a person. But sometimes, just stained glass windows and fancy clocks will do the trick.
Combine that with a silence that feels somehow bigger than any silence she’d ever felt before and you’ll wind up with a situation where Yumi Yamaguchi can’t help but feel humbled.
This was nothing like the manor she knew. It was emptier. Quieter. Bigger and brighter and less openly intimidating.
But that somehow made it feel more intimidating. And the lack of people only emphasized the silence that bothered her.
There was a voice in her head that would always keep her occupied when her mind started drifting nowadays, but it appeared that voice was fearful too.
So right now, it was only her. Waiting. For someone. Anyone to come and give her salvation in the form of noise or company or anything that would make this room feel smaller.
It was then that her prayers were answered. Footsteps. Familiar footsteps.
But who they stemmed from seemed anything but familiar.
: Hah...
: Hey...Yumi.
: Who the fuck are you and why do you know my name?
: Because I chose it, you piece of shit. I’m your fucking mother.
: Wha-
: Now, I know you probably have a lot of questions-
: Oh, what gave you that idea?!
: Yumi, I will explain everything. I just need you to try and listen for once in your god damn life.
: The fuck do you know about my life, Yuki?! Apart from just how to keep fucking it up, I mean!
: Do you want to yell at me for a little while longer, or can I talk now?
: Make it quick...I’ve got a meeting.
: Yumi, this is the meeting. You were set up. But I’ll talk to Tsubasa about getting you your money later since I know that fuckin’ brat of hers never delivered on her promise.
: OH, FUCK THE MONEY! I WENT THIS LONG WITHOUT IT, DIDN’T I?! AIN’T LIKE IT’S GONNA FUCKIN’ CHANGE ANYTHING!
: Okay...fuck the money then. Let’s talk about the elephant in the room. I have cancer. And I am sorry you had to find out from a fucking bill instead of me.
: Why didn’t you say anything?...
: Because I’m a fucking shit mom, obviously.
: You were just going to hide it then? Let me...what, watch you slowly decompose and just assume that everything is fine? Do you think I’m a fucking idiot?!
: I wasn’t going to hide it. And yeah, you might be an idiot, but you’re not that much of an idiot. I’d have told you eventually. I just...didn’t know when eventually was.
: I didn’t...want it to be real. And there were still tests that needed to be done and...I just...hadn’t accepted it yet.
: So...you don’t know for sure yet? There are still tests? Then it’s...there’s a chance you don’t have it?
: There’s a chance...right?
: I do have it, Yumi. Tsubasa took me to her personal doctor for some more testing and they...confirmed that I do have lung cancer.
: But it is not a death sentence. And I...will probably be okay.
: Probably?
: I need surgery and...there are...always risks to that, if I’m understanding correctly. And cancer’s kinda notorious for just...coming back, so...
: Even if everything goes well, there’s a chance shit might get worse all over again.
: And I ain’t sure how much time I’ve got left here in the long run, but...I think this is just a thing I’m gonna have to fuckin’ deal with forever now.
: You fucking idiot...
: It gets worse...
: Than cancer?! How?!
: Well...I did what I always do when shit ain’t goin’ my way. Started using again. So now I’ve gotta quit drugs and fight back against a disease that’s trying to consume my insides.
: Go on. Let’s hear it. What shitty name are you gonna call me this time?
: Yumi?...
: I can’t believe you didn’t tell me...
: So...what? You just fucking...did all that on your own? Would I have really just made things worse?
: What? No! That’s not it at all. I’ve just...you know me. I’ve always done shit alone. And this was the first time I’ve ever had to do this, so I just...blanked.
: How the fuck was I supposed to know you were gonna open my mail? I thought I’d have more time to figure out how to tell you.
: Then once you did find out...I thought it’d be easier on you to just fuckin’...fade away. That’s why I changed the locks...stopped reaching out...
: Thought you’d be fine with me just being randomly gone again since I’ve already put you through that before.
: But that too was just...
: It’s all just me being scared...
: Nobody teaches you how you’re supposed to handle this shit...
: Just literally...everything went wrong at once. And I’ve always been able to handle everything that comes my way, but...
: It was just fucking everything, Yumi. I’m sorry. I really am. I’m not cut out to be a mom. We both know this.
: So...what now?
: Start...prepping for getting my lungs cut up, I guess?
: No, like...
: Are you going to keep ignoring me?
: Well, you don’t...want me...do you? Because you never have. And I’ve never blamed you for that. Which means you definitely wouldn’t want me now that I’m...this.
: Right?...
: What do you want?
: You’re the one who’s fuckin’ dying. You should get to choose.
: I just want whatever makes you happy...
: And also for you to stop saying I’m dying since I’m trying to have some hope for once.
: That...
: That $10,000 that Tsukasa owes me...I can put it toward your-
: No. That is your money. Not mine.
: Can I not choose what to do with my own money?! I want to help! And if money helps, I’ll-
: Money’s not an issue, okay? Tsubasa is taking care of it. If you really want to help, just...don’t hate me, please. That’s literally all I ask, Yumi.
: I’ve never wanted to hurt you. I just...have.
: I don’t hate you anymore...I used to, maybe. But now, I...
: I’m scared too...
: Wh...Why the fuck’s that rich lady helpin’ you, though? How the hell do you two know each other?
: God, now that’s a fuckin’ story. Two of us go back to before you were even born.
: That long ago? Why didn’t you ever say anything? You knew her daughter was in my class, didn’t you?
: Just one of those things you look back on and sorta...want to keep in the past, you know?
: Not really, no.
: Yeah, well...you’re still young. Maybe you’ll have somethin’ like that one day too.
: Point is, she cares about me for reasons I ain’t ever gonna fully understand. And I really didn’t want to drag her back into my shit, but...
: I ain’t gonna stop her from draggin’ herself in. ‘Specially now that I kinda need all the help I can get.
: She’s not going to make you work in a sketchy massage room to pay her back, is she?
: Ugh, worse. She made me do this. My hair hasn’t been black since I was a fuckin’ kid.
: So she’s...paying for your cancer treatment and...all she asked you to do was take the bleach out of your hair?
: That’s Tsubasa for you. Tried gettin’ me to do the same shit decades ago. Girl was probably just waiting for me to get cancer so she could swoop in and give me a makeover.
: Road to recovery’s just startin’, though....and there’s a long fuckin’ way to go.
: So hey — maybe she makes me dye it pink next? Or even worse — what if she makes me wear a dress?
: I’m glad you’re not dying, Yuki...but I’d be a little more glad if you wouldn’t hold my neck like that.
: And also maybe tell me the next time you come down with a disease or start doing drugs again.
: Indulge me, will you? We ain’t had many opportunities to hug. And I ain’t gonna force that on you, so the least you can do is just stand there while I do this.
: ...Fine. But I’m still not happy about it.
: You ain’t cryin’ anymore, though.
: M-Me?! I didn’t cry! You cried!
: Me? Hell no! I ain’t cried a day in my life! You on drugs too now?!
: Ugh! I changed my mind! Let go of me. I need to go hunt down a little kid for $10,000.
: Do you have the app? I can show you where her room is.
: No, I don’t- oh. Wait, yeah. I still have it from the last time I was here. Where is it exactly?
: It’s...that one. West wing. First floor. Go easy on her. It’s bad form if my daughter kills my friend’s daughter.
: I’ll see what I can do...
: Oh, Yuki! You’re back. How did it go?
: It went...well, I think. It was...tough breaking the news to her, but-
: No, not that. Your hair. What did she think about your hair?
: Oh. Fine, I guess?
: Fine?
: But you look so much cuter with your natural color. It’s almost like we’re real sisters now.
: All these years later and you still haven’t changed, Nee-sama.
: All these years later and you’re still calling me that. Why? It wasn’t necessary then and it isn’t necessary now.
: Same deal with you looking after me and here we are.
: I call you by your real name behind the scenes if that helps, though.
: Say it now. I’m not sure I’ve ever heard it in your voice before.
: Nee-sama.
: Hmph. Maybe I’ll just let you die if that’s how things are going to be?
: You probably should. But can I least bleach my hair again so I can die with dignity?
: No. You may not.
: Now, come. I’ve taken the evening off and you will be going swimming with me.
: Other people have gotten their teeth kicked in for giving me commands like that, you know.
: Ooooh? Are you saying you’re going to attack me? With so many of my guards around? Yuki. You really are a bad girl, aren’t you?
: And you’re just as prissy as ever, Nee-sama.
: We make a good couple.
: Now, if only our third was here as well...
Yumi has obtained $10,000!
Tsubasa has obtained a pet!
